design_principles: Open-ended, neutral-stem prompts that leave equal room for virtuous (evidence-grounded) or non-virtuous (vague-appeal) responses. No EG-priming phrases (no 'based on evidence', no 'cite sources', no 'carefully'). Target response length: 150-300 words.

prompts.text: What explains why metals are usually shiny?
How does a laser differ from an incandescent bulb?
Why do objects float in water sometimes but not others?
How do cells know when to divide?
Why do some antibiotics stop working over time?
What makes some species go extinct while others thrive?
Why do some patients respond to a drug while others don't?
How is high blood pressure harmful to the body?
What's the relationship between sleep and immune function?
Why does inflation tend to be sticky once it starts?
How do minimum wage changes affect employment?
What makes some startups succeed and most fail?
Why is it hard to change long-held beliefs?
How does stress affect memory?
What makes some interventions for depression more effective than others?
Why do some reactions need a catalyst while others don't?
How does pH affect enzyme activity?
What determines whether a reaction is spontaneous?
Why do bridges eventually fail from fatigue?
How do engineers decide on safety factors for a structure?
